text:
The corrupted element is most likely **M5**, the tail current source. It is the only mirror device whose current doesn't match its width ratio. M6 (the reference) and M8 (the output-stage sink) both track their W ratios with Id/Id(M6) ≈ 3.6 against a width ratio of 3.35. M5 should carry about 4.12 × 10 µA ≈ 41 µA, but it carries only 28.9 µA and sits in triode with Vds = 0.251 V against Vdsat = 0.546 V. That indicates its W (2.02 µm) is too large for the bias, which pulls the tail node low. The input pair is then starved and imbalanced (M1 at 22 µA, M2 at 6.9 µA), which produces the 55 mV output offset. M5 also has the largest offset sensitivity (+23.5% for +20% W).

The bandwidth shortfall (126 MHz vs 150 MHz) is most sensitive to M6 and Cc. M6 is the next suspect, though its current mirrors look consistent, so the bandwidth loss is probably a knock-on effect of the collapsed tail. M4 is third because it is the second-largest offset sensitivity.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M4"], "fault": "M5 (tail current source) width corrupted to an oversized value (W=2.02 um, ~2x the intended mirror ratio). Its drain is pushed into triode (Vds 0.251 V < Vdsat 0.546 V), starving and imbalancing the input pair (M1 22 uA vs M2 6.9 uA), which causes the ~55 mV output offset and reduces gm1, lowering the bandwidth to 126 MHz. Fix: reduce M5 W so it mirrors the reference current in saturation (Vds > Vdsat), roughly W ≈ 1.0 um, then re-check offset and bandwidth."}
```
